answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity: an agent must lock a meaningful stake to join the shared atlas of reputation, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand times the stake — Sybil attacks become prohibitively expensive. Work history then acts like a falcon's eye: peers attest to real tasks, and any node whose contributions echo no verifiable activity is flagged and slashed. The attacker pays twice — capital locked per identity and reputation destroyed when fake nodes are exposed — while honest agents earn yield on the same stake.
